# SHSAT Test Dates 2026: Register by Oct 30—Not Dec 4


## **TL;DR**


The SHSAT test dates for Fall 2026 are November 14–15 for eligible eighth graders attending charter, private, parochial, independent, or K–12 schools, and homeschooled students; November 18 for eligible eighth graders at NYC public middle schools that end in eighth grade; and November 21 for registered ninth graders. SHSAT registration opens October 6 and closes October 30, 2026. The separate NYC high school application deadline is December 4, 2026.


Families should confirm their child's eligibility, registration status, assigned testing date, and test location through NYC Public Schools and MySchools. Missing the SHSAT registration deadline can prevent a student from taking the exam in the regular Fall 2026 admissions cycle.


This guide explains the official SHSAT schedule, registration steps, the difference between the October 30 and December 4 deadlines, the new computer-adaptive format, and how to prepare for test day.


If your child is preparing for the SHSAT or future standardized tests,[take a free diagnostic](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/diagnostic-test) to identify strengths and gaps early.


> **Quick Answer: When Is the SHSAT in 2026?**
>
>
> The Fall 2026 SHSAT is scheduled for November 14–15 for eligible eighth graders attending charter, private, parochial, independent, or K–12 schools, and homeschooled students; November 18 for eligible eighth graders at NYC public middle schools that end in eighth grade; and November 21 for registered ninth graders. Registration runs from October 6 through October 30, 2026. The separate NYC high school application deadline is December 4, 2026. Check MySchools and the official NYC Public Schools SHSAT guidance for eligibility, test assignments, and updates.

## How to Register for the SHSAT in 2026


Eligible students register for the Specialized High Schools Admissions Test through MySchools, the NYC Department of Education's online admissions portal. SHSAT registration is separate from the general high school application, even though both processes are part of the same admissions season.


### Step 1: Confirm Your Child Is Eligible


The SHSAT is for NYC residents who are currently in eighth grade or in ninth grade for the first time and are applying to a testing Specialized High School. Students must meet the eligibility requirements for the admissions cycle.


### Step 2: Sign In to MySchools


Use the official[MySchools portal](https://www.myschools.nyc/) to access the admissions process. Families who need help with account access or registration should consult NYC Public Schools.


### Step 3: Complete SHSAT Registration


Follow the current SHSAT registration instructions and complete the required steps before the October 30, 2026 deadline. Do not assume that submitting a general high school application automatically registers your child for the exam.


### Step 4: Review Your School Preferences


Review the testing Specialized High Schools available in the registration process and list preferences carefully. The order matters because offers are made using SHSAT scores and the student's ranked school preferences.


### Step 5: Check Your Test Assignment


After registration closes, check MySchools and follow NYC Public Schools' instructions for the test ticket. Confirm the assigned date, location, and any approved testing accommodations before test day.


**Registration reminder:** October 30, 2026 is the SHSAT registration deadline. December 4, 2026 is the separate deadline for the general high school and LaGuardia applications. Completing one process does not mean you have completed the other.


For the latest instructions, consult the[official NYC Public Schools Specialized High Schools page](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/enrollment/enroll-grade-by-grade/specialized-high-schools) .


## SHSAT Glossary: Key Terms Defined


### SHSAT (Specialized High Schools Admissions Test)


The standardized test used as the sole admissions criterion for eight of NYC’s nine specialized high schools. Starting Fall 2026, the SHSAT is 100 questions (50 ELA, 50 Math) administered over 180 minutes on a computer. Your child’s composite score, the combined ELA and Math scaled scores, determines whether they receive an offer.


### MySchools


The NYC Department of Education’s online portal where families register for the SHSAT and submit their high school application. Registration and the application are two separate actions on this platform, which is a critical distinction covered below.


### School Day Testing (November 18)


Eighth graders enrolled at a[public NYC middle school that ends in 8th grade test at their own school](https://ahmedprep.com/resources/2026-shsat-dates-registration-deadline) during the regular school day. This is the most common SHSAT test date, but it does not apply to every student.


### Weekend Testing (November 14-15)


Students who attend charter schools, private schools, parochial schools, independent schools, or who are homeschooled take the SHSAT at a central NYC Public Schools location on Saturday, November 14 or Sunday, November 15. Students at K-12 or 6-12 schools that don’t end in 8th grade also fall into this category.


### 9th-Grade Testing (November 21)


First-time 9th graders who are NYC residents can sit the SHSAT on Saturday, November 21 at a central location. They compete for a small number of 10th-grade seats. Students repeating 9th grade are[not eligible](https://cleverbranch.com/shsat/ninth-grade/) .


### Registration Window (October 6-30)


Twenty-five days. That is all the time families get. Registration opens on October 6 and closes on October 30. There is[no late registration and no second window](https://geniusprep.com/shsat-registration) . A student who misses this deadline cannot take the SHSAT this cycle and will not receive an offer to any testing specialized high school for September 2027 entry.


### Accommodation Documentation Deadline (October 9)


NYC Public Schools requires all accommodation paperwork submitted at least three weeks before the registration deadline. That puts the effective cutoff at[Friday, October 9, 2026](https://www.highscores.ai/shsat-prep/test-dates-and-registration/) . This applies to students with IEPs, 504 plans, or accommodation plans from non-public schools. Most competing date pages bury or skip this deadline entirely. Don’t let it sneak up on you.


### Test Ticket


Issued approximately two weeks after registration closes on October 30. The ticket confirms the student’s assigned SHSAT test date, location, and any approved accommodations. Without this ticket, your child cannot sit for the exam.


### Computer-Adaptive Test (CAT)


New for Fall 2026. The SHSAT now adjusts the difficulty of questions in real time based on how the student answers. The exam is still 180 minutes with 100 questions, and it still covers the same[grade-level standards and content areas](https://www.bettermindlabs.org/) . What changes is how students navigate through it, and this deserves its own section below.


### Composite Score


The sum of a student’s ELA scaled score and Math scaled score. NYC DOE uses this single number to rank-order all test-takers and match them to schools based on the student’s ranked preference list.


### Cutoff Score


The minimum composite score needed to receive an offer at each specialized high school. Cutoffs shift every year depending on the applicant pool. For Fall 2026 entry, the[confirmed cutoffs](https://www.shsatlab.com/blog/shsat-cutoff-scores-2026) were: Stuyvesant 561, HSMSE 539, Queens Science 531, Bronx Science 525, Staten Island Tech 517, HSAS 507, Brooklyn Tech 506, Brooklyn Latin 495.


If you want to understand how scaled scores translate to real outcomes, a[score calculator](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/score-calculator) can help build intuition about where your child needs to land.


### Offer Release (March 3, 2027)


Families learn their match after 3 PM on this date. Each student receives at most one specialized high school offer, based on their composite score and the order in which they ranked schools. There are no waitlists at the specialized high schools. Families then have roughly two to three weeks to accept or decline.


### LaGuardia (The Exception)


LaGuardia High School of Music & Art and Performing Arts is the ninth specialized high school, but it admits students by audition, not by SHSAT score. Its application deadline falls on December 4, the same as the general high school application.


## The October 30 vs. December 4 Problem


This is the single biggest source of confusion in the SHSAT admissions cycle, and it trips up families every year. Multiple top-ranking pages for SHSAT test dates now lead with this distinction in their headlines.


Here is the difference in plain terms:


**October 30** is when SHSAT registration closes. If your child wants to take the test, they must be registered by this date.


**December 4** is when the general high school application (and the LaGuardia audition application) closes. This is a completely separate step.


Registration for the SHSAT and the high school application happen on the same MySchools portal, which compounds the confusion. Practitioners on prep forums have noted that parents often see the December 4 deadline and assume they have until then to sign up for the SHSAT. They don’t. As one[SHSAT prep site puts it](https://ahmedprep.com/resources/2026-shsat-dates-registration-deadline) , “Registration is separate from the high school application, which stays open until December 4. Families should not wait for the application deadline to register for the test.”


If October 30 passes and your child isn’t registered, that’s it for this cycle.


## The 2026 Computer-Adaptive Format: What Changed


Students testing in Fall 2026 will be the[first cohort to take a computer-adaptive SHSAT](https://insideschools.org/insidetools/shsat) . This is a meaningful shift from prior years.


The evolution happened across three stages. In 2024 and earlier, the SHSAT was paper-based with 114 questions. In 2025, it went digital but stayed linear with 100 questions. Now in Fall 2026, it’s digital and adaptive with[100 questions over 180 minutes](https://www.schoolofmath.us/) .


The content hasn’t changed. Same topics, same question types, same grade-level standards. What changed is the navigation:


-


**ELA passage-based questions:** Students can review and change answers within a passage’s question set, but not after advancing to the next passage.


-


**Standalone ELA questions and all Math questions:** Students must answer each question before moving on and[cannot return to previous questions](https://honorsprep.com/blog/digital-shsat) .


This forward-only rule on Math is the biggest practical adjustment. Students who are used to skipping hard questions and coming back will need to retrain that instinct. Practicing under realistic digital, timed conditions is now essential, not just helpful.


The reassuring news: NYC Public Schools has confirmed that the scoring process and admissions logic remain unchanged. A student who has mastered the core SHSAT topics and trained on the official digital portal will be prepared regardless of what sequence the adaptive engine delivers.


Building comfort with[practice exams under test conditions](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/practice-exams) is one of the most effective ways to reduce format anxiety before test day.


## Common Mistakes Families Make


**Mistake 1: Confusing October 30 with December 4.** Covered above, but it’s worth repeating: these are two different deadlines for two different steps.


**Mistake 2: Assuming every student tests on November 18.** Only public middle school 8th graders at schools ending in 8th grade test on the school day. Charter, private, parochial, and homeschool students test on the weekend. Ninth graders test on November 21. Check your child’s category before making plans.


**Mistake 3: Missing the accommodation deadline.** October 9, not October 30. If your child needs testing accommodations, the paperwork must be in three weeks before registration closes.


**Mistake 4: Starting prep too late.** Practitioners on Reddit and prep forums consistently flag this. As one experienced SHSAT prep provider notes, “The biggest planning mistake families make is assuming SHSAT prep begins in September of eighth grade. By then, testing is only weeks away.” Students who start in the spring or summer of 7th grade give themselves time to build skills rather than cram.


**Mistake 5: Thinking you can retake in the same year.** Students can take the SHSAT[up to two times total](https://www.shsatlab.com/blog/when-is-the-shsat-2026-dates-registration-nyc) : once in 8th grade and once in 9th grade. There is no retake within the same grade year.


For students who want to start building foundational skills now, working through[targeted practice questions](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/practice-questions) in reading and math can establish a strong baseline well before October.


## What to Bring (and Leave Home) on SHSAT Test Day


**Bring:**


-


Printed test ticket (mandatory)


-


Pencils and an eraser


-


A silent watch that is not a calculator


-


Water and a quiet snack


-


Assistive technology, only if it’s listed on the student’s IEP and test ticket


**NYC Public Schools provides:**


-


The computer


-


Scrap paper


**Leave home:**


-


Cell phones and smartwatches


-


Calculators


-


Personal laptops or tablets


-


Notes or study materials


**For ELLs:** English Language Learners and eligible former ELLs receive double time, 360 minutes total, with two 15-minute breaks after the first 180 minutes.


## SHSAT Key Terms Every Family Should Know


### SHSAT


The Specialized High Schools Admissions Test is the exam used to determine admission to eight New York City specialized high schools. LaGuardia High School uses auditions instead of the SHSAT for its admissions decision.


### MySchools


MySchools is the NYC Department of Education's online admissions portal. Families use it to participate in the high school admissions process and access SHSAT registration.


### School-Day Testing


Eligible eighth graders attending NYC public middle schools that end in eighth grade take the SHSAT at their current school on the scheduled school day.


### Weekend Testing


Eligible registered eighth graders from charter, private, parochial, independent, and K–12 schools, as well as homeschooled students, take the exam at a designated central testing location on a scheduled weekend.


### Computer-Adaptive Test


A computer-adaptive test adjusts the difficulty of questions as a student responds. The Fall 2026 SHSAT uses this format while retaining 50 ELA questions, 50 Math questions, and a standard testing time of 180 minutes.


### Composite Score


The composite score combines the student's reported ELA and Math scaled scores. NYC Public Schools uses SHSAT performance and each student's ranked school preferences to determine offers to testing Specialized High Schools.


### LaGuardia High School


LaGuardia is the specialized high school that uses auditions rather than the SHSAT for admission. Its application is part of the NYC high school admissions process, with a separate application deadline from SHSAT registration.


For families thinking ahead to the SAT or ACT, many of the reading, writing, and math skills tested on the SHSAT overlap with what those exams require. Understanding[how SAT scoring works](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/how-is-the-digital-sat-scored) or exploring the[differences between the SAT and ACT](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/sat-vs-act-key-differences-how-to-choose) can help with longer-term planning.


## How to Start Preparing


The SHSAT registration window is 25 days long, but effective preparation takes months. Here’s a practical sequence:


**Step 1: Take a diagnostic.** Figure out where your child stands in both ELA and Math before spending time on anything else. A diagnostic identifies specific skill gaps so you can prioritize.


**Step 2: Build a study plan.** Map out available weeks between now and mid-November. Allocate more time to weak areas and schedule full-length practice sessions on weekends. A[study plan generator](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/study-plan-generator) can help structure the timeline.


**Step 3: Practice under digital, timed conditions.** With the new computer-adaptive format, students need to get comfortable answering questions they can’t go back to. Paper practice is no longer sufficient on its own.


**Step 4: Review and adjust.** Track scores on practice tests, identify persistent weak spots, and redirect study time accordingly.


**Step 5: Simulate test day.** In the final two weeks before the exam, run full 180-minute sessions with proper timing, breaks, and a realistic setup. This builds both stamina and confidence.


[Start with a free diagnostic test](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/diagnostic-test) to see where your child’s skills stand today.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### When is the SHSAT in 2026?


The SHSAT has multiple test dates in Fall 2026. Weekend testing is November 14-15 for charter, private, parochial, and homeschool 8th graders. School day testing is November 18 for public middle school 8th graders. Ninth-grade testing is November 21.


### When does SHSAT registration close?


Friday, October 30, 2026. This is a hard deadline with no late registration and no exceptions. Registration opens on October 6.


### Can you take the SHSAT in 9th grade?


Yes. First-time 9th graders who are NYC residents can take the SHSAT on November 21, 2026 and compete for a limited number of 10th-grade seats. Students repeating 9th grade are not eligible.


### Is there late registration for the SHSAT?


No. NYC Public Schools does not offer late registration, a second registration window, or any exceptions after October 30. If you miss it, your child cannot test this cycle.


### When do SHSAT scores and offers come out?


Offers are released on Wednesday, March 3, 2027, after 3 PM. NYC DOE does not release individual SHSAT scores separately from the offer process.


### Is the SHSAT computer-adaptive now?


Yes. Starting Fall 2026, the SHSAT uses a computer-adaptive format where question difficulty adjusts based on student responses. The test is still 100 questions (50 ELA, 50 Math) over 180 minutes, and the content remains the same.


### What is the accommodation deadline for the SHSAT?


Friday, October 9, 2026. All accommodation documentation must be submitted at least three weeks before the October 30 registration deadline.


### What is the difference between October 30 and December 4?


October 30 is when SHSAT registration closes. December 4 is when the general high school application and LaGuardia audition application close. These are two separate deadlines for two separate steps. Do not wait until December 4 to register for the SHSAT.
